text: For the Energy theme, the highest-priority Layer 2 work should start with grid hardware, dry-type transformers, utility structures and second-order grid suppliers before broad utilities or commodity producers.
PLPC, HPS.A, ACA, VMI and AZZ form the initial underfollowed electricity-infrastructure cluster, spanning line hardware, transformers, structures and coatings.

LEU, BWXT and HON form a separate nuclear-fuel bottleneck cluster, but public-market exposure quality is mixed because conversion and HALEU capacity are policy-dependent and not cleanly investable through one pure-play listed company.

Layer 1C remains narrow outside electricity infrastructure; run dedicated Layer 1B expansion for oil/gas services, LNG equipment, midstream compression, refining equipment, renewable interconnection, storage and switchgear.
Next pass should verify market caps, analyst coverage counts, backlog visibility, customer concentration and segment purity before promoting candidates to deeper Serenity evidence validation.

Energy theme should be split first into electricity infrastructure, nuclear fuel chain, renewables/grid integration, and oil/gas before ranking securities. Current Layer 2A has strongest evidence for electricity infrastructure and nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks.

Highest-scoring bottleneck nodes: customer qualification/audits, high-voltage/HVDC equipment, HALEU/enrichment, transformers/power-quality equipment, switchgear/power distribution, uranium conversion, transmission hardware, and utility procurement.

Low-attention bottleneck value may hide in transmission line hardware, utility structures, galvanizing/coatings, dry-type transformer suppliers, high-voltage component suppliers, procurement systems, testing/certification, and approval-heavy suppliers rather than only in utilities, IPPs, mega-cap industrials, or EPC leaders.

Catalysts to track: transformer and switchgear lead-time commentary, utility T&D capex updates, large-load interconnection policy, high-voltage customer audits, data-center customer wins, utility-structure backlog, HALEU/DOE funding, and advanced nuclear fuel fabrication licensing or offtake.

Need primary-source verification from 10-Ks, annual reports, investor presentations, earnings transcripts, utility procurement documents, DOE/FERC/NRC filings, and customer announcements before advancing specific companies to later Serenity layers.

Oil and gas chain remains under-mapped. Follow-on Layer 2A pass should split upstream services, pressure pumping, compression, LNG liquefaction equipment, midstream, specialty valves, inspection/testing, refinery equipment, and emissions/measurement systems.

Renewables chain remains under-mapped. Follow-on pass should separate interconnection queues, inverters, trackers, storage, grid-forming equipment, HVDC, transformer access, renewable O&M, and power-market/regulatory constraints.

Need to verify market caps, analyst coverage, revenue exposure purity, backlog, book-to-bill, customer concentration, and named customer evidence for underfollowed candidates before treating them as durable bottleneck candidates.
PLPC should be tracked as an early-order signal for transmission buildout, with a possible 6-12 month lead versus downstream EPC and utility construction activity.
HPS.A is a cleaner physical-power bottleneck than HON for AI infrastructure screening because it sits in transformers and power-quality equipment rather than a diluted mega-cap conversion asset.
Need company filings and transcripts to quantify backlog, customer concentration, and lead-time signals for PLPC, HPS.A, ACA, VMI, and AZZ before promoting any of them to later Serenity layers.
Need to verify how much of HON's conversion asset is economically material, and whether LEU or BWXT better captures the investable nuclear bottleneck depending on policy and contract visibility.
